sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File header note
sections.what: The header says this is a client for the Resend email service that sends hiring manager and CEO outreach emails, and links to the vendor's send-email documentation.
sections.why: Stated in the header: it explains the file's purpose and points to the vendor reference.
sections.watch_out: The header says it sends real emails, so callers must make sure a person has approved each draft before sending.

sections.name: ResendSendParams
sections.title: Fields needed to send an email
sections.what: Describes the information needed to send one email through the Resend email service: sender, recipient, subject, body, and optional reply, copy, and blind copy addresses.
sections.why: Gives the app one shared shape for emails, so a missing or misspelled field is caught by the editor.
sections.watch_out: The sender address must belong to a domain verified in Resend. This type cannot check that.

sections.name: ResendResponse
sections.title: Reply from the email service
sections.what: Describes the reply Resend sends after accepting an email, which is an identifier for the sent message.
sections.why: Lets the caller keep a reference to each sent email. Any further reason is not stated in the code.

sections.name: sendEmail
sections.title: Sending one email
sections.what: Sends one email by calling Resend with the caller's key. It refuses to run without a key or sender address, and throws an error with the status code if Resend rejects the request.
sections.why: The error messages point the owner to the settings page where the key and sender are entered.
sections.watch_out: The key is passed in by the caller, and this file does not say whether it runs on the server. If it runs in the browser, the key is exposed.
